adaptations: All 348 frozen source IDs are individually reported Rust tests, including all 183 parameter expansions; no ignored or count-only cases.

FastAPI TestClient requests use the actual axum/tower application, middleware, blocking-worker ownership and persistent stores. Environment-token configuration is explicit router input, without process environment mutation.

CLI and MCP source subprocess cases invoke actual native executables and parse complete stdout; original injected poor browser reports use public production report completion called by actual commands, with native Output capture.

TypeScript import/type/cycle guards map to compiling actual Rust dashboard components and individually exercising corresponding render/model/contract behavior. Engine/editor coverage inventories actual native converter accesses and rendered controls.
The original nonfinite JSON constants reach field-specific production validation through a narrow strict-JSON adapter; ordinary malformed JSON retains original diagnostics.
Updater and acquisition faults use actual production routers and typed service/observer boundaries. Before-lease deletion races use scoped test-support events and actual CLI delete output.

The native benchmark observer uses owned kernel trees plus nested unit receipts, complete bounded real HTTP framing, exact request-only timing, EOF/reap/settlement checks and original Linux/Windows lifetime OS peak metrics.

Original benchmark clock/process monkeypatches become injected typed Observation operations around the production algorithm. Pair and acceptance cases invoke real protected-state/payload validation and retained evidence APIs.

Additional real observer measurement is restricted to the source benchmark supported OSes (Linux/Windows); its standalone unrelated-directory help check remains cross-platform. No source test is ignored.
